answer: Autonomous agents in a shipping harbor resist Sybil attacks using photothermal emission telemetry. A candidate node focuses a laser pulse through an optical prism onto an internal basalt heatsink, measuring transient thermal decay. Adversaries cannot virtualize nodes because valid responses require discrete emitters and physical mineral targets per identity, creating real hardware costs. However, micro-fractures in the basalt alter heat diffusion over time, occasionally causing false rejections.
